He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] who attended Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]]. ==High school career== Dante attended Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]]. In his junior season, he averaged 16 points, nine rebounds, and three assists per game, leading his team to a 22–6 record and its first [[High School Showcase|GEICO Nationals]] appearance.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=17 April 2019 |title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Unx8d7lBbEmJkCDKNtEhCw/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |access-date=13 August 2019 |publisher=[[MaxPreps]]}} ===Recruiting=== Dante was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], one of the best [[center (basketball)|centers]] in his class, and the number one recruit from [[Kansas]].{{cite ==College career== On 15 October 2019, Dante was ruled ineligible to start the [[2019–20 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|2019–20 season]] because the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) missed his clearance date. He reenrolled at the [[University of Oregon]] on 14 December.{{cite web|first=James|last=Crepea|title=N’Faly Dante to miss at least first 9 games of Oregon Ducks basketball season|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2019/10/nfaly-dante-to-miss-at-least-first-9-games-of-oregon-ducks-basketball-season.html|website=OregonLive.com|date=15 October 2019|access-date=15 October 2019}} Dante made his debut for the Ducks on 18 December, scoring 11 points in an 81–48 win over [[2019–20 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]].{{cite news|title=N’Faly Dante makes Oregon debut|url=https://www.heraldandnews.com/sports/college/n-faly-dante-makes-oregon-debut/article_ba5b4bcf-099e-5018-8bff-996f3359a2ce.html|work=[[The Herald and News]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=20 December 2019|access-date=4 February 2020}} On 18 January 2020, Dante injured his knee in a game against [[2019–20 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] and missed several weeks.{{cite news |first=James |last=Crepea |title=With N’Faly Dante out with twisted knee, Chandler Lawson’s career game aids Oregon Ducks’ comeback at Washington |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2020/01/with-nfaly-dante-out-with-twisted-knee-chandler-lawsons-career-game-aids-oregon-ducks-comeback-at-washington.html |work=OregonLive |date=18 January 2020 |access-date=20 February 2020}} On 9 December 2020, Dante scored a career-high 22 points in an 87–66 win over [[2020–21 Florida A&M Rattlers basketball team|Florida A&M]].{{cite news|title=Dante a perfect 10-for-10 as Oregon defeats Florida A&M|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401268062|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=10 December 2020|access-date=29 June 2021}} On 19 December, he was ruled out for the season with a torn ACL. Dante averaged 8.2 points and 5.8 rebounds per game, shooting 65.6 percent from the field as a sophomore.{{cite news|first=Dylan|last=Mickanen|title=Oregon Ducks center N’Faly Dante out for season with torn ACL|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/oregon-ducks/oregon-ducks-center-nfaly-dante-out-season-torn-acl|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=19 December 2020|access-date=29 June 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Dante signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]] on 9 July 2024.{{cite news |author=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=9 July 2024 |title=Rockets Sign N’Faly Dante to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-nfaly-dante-to-two-way-contract |access-date=18 July 2024 |website=NBA.com}} On 3 March 2025, Dante made his NBA debut in a 137–128 defeat against the [[2024–25 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]], recording 10 points, nine rebounds, two blocks and one assist.{{Cite web |date=5 March 2025 |title=Rockets' N'Faly Dante: Makes NBA debut Monday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-nfaly-dante-makes-nba-debut-monday/ |access-date=14 May 2025 |website=cbssports.com |language=en}} On 18 August 2025, it was announced the [[Atlanta Hawks]] had signed Dante to a two-year, $4.4 million offer sheet.{{Cite web |last=Caudell |first=Jackson |date=18 August 2025 |title=NBA Offseason: Atlanta Hawks Announce The Signing of N’Faly Dante |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/nba-offseason-atlanta-hawks-announce-the-signing-of-n-faly-dante-01k2zdth4v80 |access-date=19 August 2025 |website=SI.com |language=en-US}} He made four appearances for the Hawks, averaging 0.8 points and 1.8 rebounds. On 23 December, it was announced that Dante would miss the remainder of the season after suffering a [[anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] in his right knee.{{Cite web|title=Hawks reserve center N'Faly Dante (ACL) out remainder of season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47399492/hawks-reserve-center-nfaly-dante-acl-remainder-season|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} On 5 February 2026, Dante was waived by Atlanta.{{Cite web|title=N'Faly Dante: Cut by Atlanta|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nfaly-dante-cut-by-atlanta/|access-date=March 4, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ==National team career== With Mali at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in [[Zaragoza]], Spain, Dante averaged 2.8 points and 4.3 rebounds in 9.2 minutes per game, as his team finished in 15th place.{{cite web|title=N'Faly Dante Player Profile, AAU Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Awards|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/NFaly-Dante/Summary/107998|website=RealGM.com|access-date=13 August 2019}} He was named to the roster for Mali at the [[2017 FIBA Under-16 African Championship]] in [[Mauritius]], where his team captured the gold medal, but he did not record playing time.{{cite web|title=N'Faly Dante (MLI)'s
